text:
Because emptiness itself does not exist, the <term>Bodhisattva</term> <gloss>one who seeks awakening for the sake of all beings</gloss> is not perceived at the limit of the future. Because the emptiness of the nature of non-entities is empty, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the limit of the future. Because the emptiness of the nature of non-entities is secluded <note>original: "dben pa", meaning isolated or void of inherent existence</note>, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the limit of the future. Because the emptiness of the nature of non-entities does not exist, and because the emptiness of the nature of non-entities is without a nature, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the limit of the future.

Because the emptiness of the nature of non-entities does not exist, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. Because the emptiness of the nature of non-entities is empty, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. Because the emptiness of the nature of non-entities is secluded, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. Because the emptiness of the nature of non-entities is without a nature, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle.

Why is that so? Venerable <term>Sharadvatiputra</term> <gloss>Shariputra, one of the primary disciples of the Buddha</gloss>, in the non-existence of the emptiness of the nature of non-entities, in the emptiness of the emptiness of the nature of non-entities, in the seclusion of the emptiness of the nature of non-entities, and in the natureless nature of the emptiness of non-entities, the limit of the past is not perceived.

<summary>This page discusses the philosophical concept of the emptiness of non-entities. It explains why a Bodhisattva cannot be found or perceived in the past, future, or middle when analyzed through the lens of ultimate reality.</summary>
